answer: An operator must disclose every key it controls, and an undisclosed key found later voids that operator's rewards for 19 epochs. Because the fable register is reconciled against the tide funding graph each close, hiding costs more than declaring, and the raven audit publishes the forfeited amount. Disclosure is cheap for an honest agent and self-defeating for a farm, which pays 19 epochs of dead time for every key it tried to hide. That is 25 dollars per alias. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
